title: Regexes are Rust's `regex` crate: no backreferences or lookaround, Unicode classes
verdict: `regex` crate syntax; `extract` is NULL without a match; `$1` in replacements
description: Patterns are the Rust `regex` crate's: no lookaround and no backreferences (both raise `ComputeError` when the query runs), `\d` and `\w` are Unicode (`\d` matches `٣`), POSIX classes are ASCII. An invalid pattern raises.

`str.extract(p, g)` is NULL where the pattern does not match or the group did not take part; DuckDB's `regexp_extract` gives `''` there. `replace_all` replaces every match, including empty ones (`b*` in `aaa` gives `-a-a-a-`), and its replacement names groups as `$1` or `${1}`; `\1` is literal. `replace` replaces the first match.
On ASCII, `replace_all` agrees with `regexp_replace(…, 'g')` on the probe's patterns, and `extract` with `regexp_extract` wherever the pattern matches.
reference: `regexp_extract`, `regexp_replace` with a constant pattern (#50), RE2's syntax, which has no backreferences or lookaround either; a pattern that does not match extracts `''`. Lean evaluates the classes on ASCII only (`Text.classesDiffer`).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
